full_judgment:
Bimalendu Bikash Roy Choudhury J: This appeal, at the instance of the Chairman, Chittagong Port Authority, is directed against the judgment dated 30 January 1992 of the High Court Division, Admiralty jurisdiction passed on compromise in Admiralty Suit No. 27 of 1991 allowing MV Fong Yun (defendant No.1) to leave the territorial waters of Bangladesh without payment of the dues and other charges of the Port Authority. The appeal is by way of leave under Article 103(3) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, which is limited to a question of law. The question involved is whether the learned Admiralty Judge acted beyond his jurisdiction in allowing the said vessel MV Fong Yun to leave the territorial waters of Bangladesh without payment of the port dues and other charges of the Chittagong Port Authority, while passing the compromise decree. 

 2. The matter has arisen in this way. The vessel MV Fong Yun arrived at the outer anchorage of the Chittagong Port on 30 July 1990. On 3 August 1991 while entering into Chittagong Port from the outer anchorage the said vessel collided with Bangladesh Naval Frigate BNS Osman and caused extensive damage thereto. On 14 August 1991 Ministry of Defence of the Government of Bangladesh and Commodore Commanding BN Flotilla as plaintiffs brought the aforementioned suit against the vessel, her master, agents and others for recovery of US Dollar 23,918 million equivalent to Taka 88,49,66,000.00 as compensation for causing the damage to the Bangladesh Naval Frigate upon allegation that the vessel MV Fong Yun recklessly negotiated itself so as to cause the damage. Upon a petition the plaintiffs secured the arrest of the vessel and had it held up at the Chittagong Port for a certain period. Meanwhile the plaintiffs and the principal defendants filed a joint application for disposal of the suit in terms of compromise between the parties. The terms and conditions of the compromise were to the effect that the defendants would pay to the first plaintiff. Ministry of Defence a sum of US. $ 2.4 million (US $ 24,00,000) in full and final settlement of the plaintiffs' claim, that the payment would be made by transfer into a certain specified account of Bangladesh Bank, whereupon Bangladesh Bank would furnish written confirmation of the receipt of the money of the Attorney General, and that the ship would be entitled to be released and allowed to leave the territorial waters of Bangladesh with her belongings, master and crew, that the plaintiffs would then procure immediate release of the vessel with her belongings, master and crew from arrest and detention and ensure her sailing out from Chittagong and also procure withdrawal of all proceedings now pending before the courts in Bangladesh and would keep harmless the ship against future arrest or detention in connection with the incident in question. 

 3. While passing the decree the Admiralty Judge, upon a verbal submission on behalf of the vessel that since in pursuance of an amicable settlement the claims of the plaintiff had been satisfied, the vessel which was under arrest since 15 September 1991 might be exempted from payment of all port dues and other charges of the Chittagong Port Authority which had accrued and was to accrue till the date of her release, ordered, amongst other things, that the vessel MV Fong Yun "be allowed to leave the territorial waters of Bangladesh immediately with her master, crew and her belongings without payment of the port dues and other charges of the Port authority. Proforma defendant Nos. 5, 6 & 7 and all other concerned authorities are directed to give effect to this order immediately". It transpires that though the appellant was a proforma party to the suit he did not enter appearance. And no decree was passed against him ex parte.
